question: What does a recipient of revocable permission owe before its own organisation of reliance makes ending the permitted use morally costly?
rejected_broad_novelty_claims: Moral duties can be manufactured by another person
Exit costs should be fairly allocated
Valid consent can coexist with wronging
closest_checked: Keller 2018, complete publisher web article body
closest_not_fully_checked: Liberto 2022: chapter 2 abstract and opening preview only
Sun 2025: indexed excerpts; full retrieval blocked
proposed_increment: An argument and bounded recipient-specific prospective rule for avoidable, unapproved creation of morally binding exit burdens, with separate treatment of validity, cessation, current rescue and restoration; extends beyond manipulative intent and actual withdrawal.
strongest_rival: Reasonable reliance and valuable interdependence can permissibly change what the consenter owes; normative revocation never implied an unqualified liberty to withdraw support.
tests_to_answer_in_manuscript: same beneficiary welfare and no manipulative motive
third-party rescue duty survives wrongful setup
ordinary coordination and inherent exit costs
complaint before withdrawal and while still content to consent
